speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
translit: senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṁ sthāpaya me ’chyuta
theme: Arjuna Asks Krishna to Pause the Chariot
hindi: अर्जुन ने हृषीकेश श्रीकृष्ण से कहा: “हे अच्युत! मेरा रथ दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में खड़ा कर दीजिए।” संजय राजा धृतराष्ट्र को यह बात बता रहे हैं।
english: Sanjaya tells the king that Arjuna then spoke to Krishna, the Lord of the senses. Arjuna said, “O Achyuta, please place my chariot in the middle between the two armies.”
deeper: Arjuna is a great archer with his bow raised, and the conches have just sounded. Yet he does not rush forward. He asks to be taken to the middle, where he can see both armies clearly. Before a big step, he wants to see the whole picture.

Look at how he speaks. He calls Krishna Hrishikesha, the master of the senses, and Achyuta, the one who never falls or fails. Krishna is his charioteer, but Arjuna trusts him like a close friend and guide. A wise person asks for help from someone steady and trustworthy.

This small request is where the whole Gita begins to turn. In the middle of the field, Arjuna will soon see faces he knows, and his heart will be shaken. A pause to look honestly can show us things that are hard to feel. That is often the first step toward real understanding.
words: to Hrishikesha (Krishna), the master of the senses
O Lord of the Earth (O King)
O Achyuta, the one who never falls
background: The conches of both sides had been sounding. The Pandava conches rang so loudly that the sky and earth echoed and the hearts of Dhritarashtra’s sons trembled (1.19). The armies stood ready, and weapons were about to begin their clash (1.20).

Then Arjuna, whose flag carried Hanuman, looked at Dhritarashtra’s sons standing in battle order. He lifted his bow and spoke to Krishna (1.20). This verse gives us his words: he asks Krishna to drive the chariot to the middle of the field.
lessons: Even when everyone is ready to rush, Arjuna stops to look carefully first.
Standing in the middle helps us see both sides instead of only our own.
Arjuna turns to Krishna, a steady friend, when he needs direction.
Arjuna makes his request plainly and with respect, calling Krishna Achyuta.
When we look closely at a difficult situation, our feelings may surprise us, and that is part of learning.
examples: Aarav’s friend breaks his pencil box by mistake. Aarav feels like shouting, but he stops and takes a deep breath first. He then hears what really happened.
Two classmates in Pune argue about who spoiled the group project. Their monitor, Sana, listens to both before saying anything.
Kavya is unsure whether to tell the teacher about a friend’s mistake. She quietly asks her class teacher for advice instead of deciding in a hurry.
Before the cricket match in the gully, captain Rohan looks at the whole ground. He checks where each fielder stands before he starts the game.
Meena stops at the middle of the lane and looks both ways before she cycles across. A few seconds of looking keep her safe.
Before exams, Dev sits with his father and looks at the whole syllabus. They see what is easy and what is hard, then make a plan.
At Diwali, two cousins fight over a sparkler box. Their grandmother calls them to sit between her and asks each to tell their side calmly.
Ishita notices she has been unkind to a new girl, Farah. It feels uncomfortable to admit, but looking honestly helps her say sorry.

story.title: The Kite on the Terrace
paras: In a lane in Jaipur, a bright orange kite landed on Mr. Sharma’s terrace. Two groups of children both claimed it. Kabir’s group said they had cut it down, and Zoya’s group said it was theirs from the start. Voices rose, and some hands were already reaching for the string.

Kabir was the captain of his group. His heart was thumping, and he felt ready to push ahead. Then he remembered something his elder brother Arjun always said: “Before you fight, stand in the middle and look.” He asked his brother to walk with him to the middle of the lane.

From there, Kabir could see both groups. He saw Zoya’s little brother near tears. He saw that some of his own friends were only shouting because others were shouting. Arjun said gently, “Now tell me what you see.” Kabir felt his anger slowly cool down.

Kabir called out, “Let us ask Mr. Sharma to bring the kite down, and then we can decide fairly.” Mr. Sharma smiled, and the kite was cut in two halves and shared. Soon both groups were flying kites together.
story.moral: Lesson: When things get heated, pause, ask a trusted guide, and look at the whole picture before you act.

quiz.q: What did Arjuna ask Krishna to do in this verse?
o: Place the chariot between the two armies
quiz.x: Arjuna asked Krishna to station the chariot in the middle between both armies.

quiz.q: What does the name Achyuta mean?
o: The one who never falls or fails
quiz.x: Achyuta means the unfallen, one who never slips from his greatness.

quiz.q: Who is telling the king these words in the story?
quiz.x: Sanjaya narrates the events of the battlefield to King Dhritarashtra.

quiz.q: What can we learn from Arjuna asking to go to the middle?
o: Pause and see the whole picture before acting
Only look at your own side
quiz.x: Going to the middle shows the wish to see clearly before taking a big step.

reel.hook: Why did Arjuna stop the chariot right before the big battle?
reel.lesson: Pause and look at the whole picture before you act.
reel.caption:
Arjuna had his bow raised, yet he asked Krishna to stop in the middle and look first. 🛞
Next time you feel like rushing, try a pause. It helps you see clearly.
What will you pause for today? 🌟
